```{r}
raw_station <- read_excel(here("data", "updated", "tucker_station.xlsx"))
```

Adding year and month columns, changing all TT station to MW (used interchangeably in cruises)

Excluding egg, nauplii, and protozoea.

Adding length and width mean and bins

Adding length bin and total jar count and density number columns:

Note: zoea will lose the range but zoea data is not used in size analyses

```{r}
data_jars <- clean_names(raw_size) %>%  
  
  filter(!type %in% c("egg", "nauplii", "protozoea")) %>%
  
   mutate(year = 2000 + as.numeric(substr(cruise, 4, 5)),
        month = as.numeric(substr(cruise, 6, 7)),
        
        station = case_when(station == "TT" ~ "MW",
         TRUE ~ station),
              
        season = case_when(
             month %in% c(1, 2, 3) ~ "JFM",
             month %in% c(4, 5, 6) ~ "AMJ",
             month %in% c(7, 8, 9) ~ "JAS",
             month %in% c(10, 11, 12) ~ "OND"),
        
       length_bin = (floor(length_l)),
       length_mid = (length_l + length_h) / 2,
       width_mid = (width_l + width_h) / 2) %>%
  
  relocate(length_mid, .after = length_h) %>%
  relocate(width_mid, .after = width_h) %>%
  relocate(length_bin, .after= length_l) %>%
  relocate(year, .after = date) %>%
  relocate(month, .after = year) %>%
  relocate(season, .after = month) %>%
  
  
  group_by(id_jar) %>%
    mutate(
         dens_jar = sum(dens_number, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
    ungroup()
```

Preparing station data: to do: ME mentioned seconds in some emails. Check if that is a column in data files

Changing all TT station to MW (used interchangeably in cruises)

Defining time values as hms time format.

Changing depth values to absolute numbers instead of negative.

Adding "diel" column to differentiate day and night samples: samples collected between 6am and 6pm are considered day samples, otherwise, night. to do: check sunrise and sunset times for data that has a closer hour to 6pm/6am

```{r}
data_station <- clean_names(raw_station) %>%
 
  
  mutate(
    time_in = hms::as_hms(time_in),
    time_out = hms::as_hms(time_out),

    open_mid = na_if(open_mid, "DNF"),
    open_mid = hms::as_hms(as.numeric(open_mid) * 86400),
    
    open_top = na_if(open_top, "DNF"),
    open_top = hms::as_hms(as.numeric(open_top) * 86400), 
    
    hour = hour(time_in),
    
    diel = case_when(
         hour >= 6 & hour < 18 ~ "day",
         hour >= 18 | hour < 6 ~ "night", TRUE ~ NA_character_),
  

    depth_mean = abs(depth_mean),
    depth_min = abs(depth_min),
    depth_max = abs(depth_max),
    
    station = case_when(station == "TT" ~ "MW",
      TRUE ~ station)) 

```

model summary table color coding functions

to do: check the placement of this and in general if the code makes sense

```{r}
color_col <- function(x) {pal <- c("#d73027", "#fc8d59", "#fee08b", "#1a9850") 
  
  ranks <- rank(x, ties.method = "average")
  bins <- cut(
    ranks,
    breaks = 4,
    labels = pal,
    include.lowest = TRUE)
  
  cell_spec(round(x, 3), background = as.character(bins), color = "black")}

color_col_low_good <- function(x) {
  pal <- c("#1a9850", "#fee08b", "#fc8d59", "#d73027")
  # green, yellow, orange, red
  
  ranks <- rank(x, ties.method = "average")
  bins <- cut(
    ranks,
    breaks = 4,
    labels = pal,
    include.lowest = TRUE)
  
  cell_spec(round(x, 3), background = as.character(bins), color = "black")}

```

Excluding cruises from February (n=1), and October (n=3).

NOTE: April (n=2) only includes night and nearshore-day samples. in theory, April samples would be valid when the time resolution is seasons (included in spring/AMJ) but seasonal comparisons are often for day/off shore samples, therefore April samples are excluded as a result of filtering for sampling time and location.

Excluding samples collected at night - insufficient for analysis: day: 424 jars night: 117 jars

Excluding nearshore samples - insufficient for analysis: offshore = 405 jars nearshore = 33 jars

Changing all imm m to m, and imm f to f for consistency (some samples include rows labeled as m in lower than 11mm ranges) to do: check this since new data has corrections in assigned life stage

Keeping only juvenile and adult data NOTE: unsexed adults (type = "adult") will be included in analyses which group all adults together, but excluded when females and males are being compared.

Filtering size to exclude zoea.

Only including numerically dominant species -- Euphausia pacifica (EPAC), Nematoscelis difficilis (NDIF), Thysanoessa spinifera (TSPIN), excluding euphausiidae).

to do: would be interesting to model all euphausiid adults regardless of species or sex, this way unidentifies euphausiidae will also be included.

Total valid jars: 541

```{r}
data_krill <- data_all %>%
  
  filter(
      ! month %in% c(2, 10),
      diel == "day",
      ! station %in% c("EX", "E", "ME", "ME/EX", "M/ME", "M", "Mew", ".", "N/A")) %>%
  
  
  mutate(type = case_when(
      type == "imm m" ~ "m",
      type == "imm f" ~ "f",
      TRUE ~ type)) %>%
  
  filter(type %in% c("juv", "f", "m", "adult"),
         length_l > 4,
  
          species_name %in% c(
           "EUP Euphausia pacifica",
           "EUP Nematoscelis difficilis",
           "EUP Thysanoessa spinifera")) %>%
  
  mutate(
    species_code = case_when(
      species_name == "EUP Euphausia pacifica" ~ "EPAC",
      species_name == "EUP Thysanoessa spinifera" ~ "TSPIN",
      species_name == "EUP Nematoscelis difficilis" ~ "NDIF")) 
```

calculating weighted mean length using density number in each jar for each species/type:

- tot_dens shows the sum of density number in the jar - total number of euphausiids in the jar divided by volume of filtered water also accounting for on-board subsampling.
- n_rows shows the number of rows that were consolidated in each jar

Here, each jar has one value per species/type (max rows for a jar is 9)

```{r}
data_meanlen_jar <- data_krill %>%
  
  filter(
    is.finite(length_mid),
    is.finite(dens_number)) %>%
  
  group_by(id_jar, moci_cencal, moci_norcal, species_code, type, dens_jar, line, pdo, npgo) %>%
  
  summarise(
    mean_length = weighted.mean(length_mid, w = dens_number),
    n_rows = n(),
    
    .groups = "drop")
```


creating dataset of annual length median and Q3 of each specie: showing the 50th and 75th percentile of the pooled, equally weighted jar-level length distributions for each species and year.

```{r}
length_summary <- data_krill %>%

  filter(!is.na(length_mid)) %>%

  group_by(id_jar, species_code) %>%
  mutate(
    dens_species = sum(dens_number, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%

  
  filter(dens_species > 0) %>%

  group_by(year, species_code, length_mid) %>%
  summarise(
    frequency = sum(dens_number / dens_species, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop" ) %>%

  
  
  arrange(year, species_code, length_mid) %>%

  group_by(year, species_code) %>%
  mutate(
    cumulative_frequency = cumsum(frequency),
    total_frequency = sum(frequency, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%

  
  summarise(
    median_length = length_mid[
      which(cumulative_frequency >= total_frequency * 0.50)[1]],
    
    q3_length = length_mid[
      which(cumulative_frequency >= total_frequency * 0.75)[1]],
    
    .groups = "drop")
```

creating dataset of cruise-level length median and Q3 of each species: showing the 50th and 75th percentile of the pooled, equally weighted jar-level length distributions for each species and cruise.

```{r}
length_sum_cruise <- data_krill %>%

  filter(!is.na(length_mid)) %>%

  group_by(id_jar, species_code) %>%

    frequency = sum(dens_number / dens_species, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop" ) %>%

```

## Codes

### Annual bar

Annual length bar plot, with env factor line. (x: year, y: length)

```{r}
plot_length_env <- function(data, species, metric, env_data, env_var) {

  length_df <- data %>%
    filter(species_code == species)

  plot_df <- length_df %>%
    left_join(
      env_data %>% select(year, all_of(env_var)),
      by = "year")

  
  # Labels
  metric_label <- ifelse(metric == "median_length", "Median", "Q3")

  env_label <- toupper(env_var)

  
  # Secondary axis transformation
  length_range <- range(plot_df[[metric]], na.rm = TRUE)
  env_range <- range(plot_df[[env_var]], na.rm = TRUE)

  scale_factor <- diff(length_range) / diff(env_range)
  offset <- length_range[1] - env_range[1] * scale_factor

  padding <- diff(length_range) * 0.10
  y_limits <- c(
  length_range[1] - padding,
  length_range[2] + padding)
  
  
 ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = factor(year))) +

  # Body length bars
  geom_col(
    aes(y = .data[[metric]]),
    fill = species_colors[species],
    width = 0.7,
    alpha = 0.8) +

   
  # Environmental index line
  geom_line(
    aes(y = .data[[env_var]] * scale_factor + offset, group = 1),
    color = env_colors[env_var],
    linewidth = 1,
    na.rm = TRUE) +

  geom_point(
    aes(y = .data[[env_var]] * scale_factor + offset),
    color = env_colors[env_var],
    size = 2,
    na.rm = TRUE) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    name = paste0(metric_label, " body length (mm)"),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(
      ~ (. - offset) / scale_factor,
      name = env_label
    )
  ) +
   
   
scale_x_discrete(drop = TRUE)  +
   
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    title =  paste0( "Annual " ,
      species, ": ", metric_label,
      " body length vs. ", env_label)) +

   
  theme_classic() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.y.left = element_text(color = "black"),
    axis.title.y.right = element_text(color = "black")
  )}
```

## Cruise-level scatter

Cruise level scatter plots (x: env factor, y: length)

```{r}
plot_length_scatter <- function(data, species, metric, env_var) {


plot_df <- data %>%
  filter(species_code == species) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(.data[[env_var]]),
    is.finite(.data[[metric]])
  )

p_value <- cor.test(
  plot_df[[env_var]],
  plot_df[[metric]],
  method = "pearson"
)$p.value

p_color <- ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "forestgreen", "#a91b0d")

  # Labels
  metric_label <- ifelse(metric == "median_length", "Median", "Q3")
  env_label <- toupper(env_var)

  ggplot(plot_df,
         aes(x = .data[[env_var]], y = .data[[metric]])) +

    geom_point(
      color = species_colors[species],
      size = 2.5,
      alpha = 0.8,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +

    geom_smooth(
      method = "lm",
      formula = y ~ x,
      se = TRUE,
      color = env_colors[env_var],,
      fill = env_colors[env_var],,
      alpha = 0.2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    
    # Regression equation
    stat_regline_equation(
      aes(label = after_stat(eq.label)),
      label.x.npc = "left",
      label.y.npc = 0.98
    ) +

# Pearson r
stat_cor(
  method = "pearson",
  aes(label = after_stat(r.label)),
  label.x.npc = "left",
  label.y.npc = 0.88,
  color = "black"
) +

# P-value
stat_cor(
  method = "pearson",
  aes(label = after_stat(p.label)),
  label.x.npc = "left",
  label.y.npc = 0.80,
  color = p_color
) +

    labs(
      x = env_label,
      y = paste0(metric_label, " body length (mm)"),
      title = paste0(
        species, ": ", metric_label,
        " body length vs. ", env_label
      )
    ) +

    theme_classic() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
      axis.text = element_text(size = 12)
    )
}
```

## Side-by-side

combining bars and scatter:

```{r}
plot_length_combined <- function(data1, data2, species, metric,
                                 env_data, env_var,
                                 widths = c(8, 10)) {

  # Labels
  metric_label <- ifelse(metric == "median_length", "Median", "Q3")
  env_label <- toupper(env_var)

  # Shared body length limits
  y_limits <- range(
    c(
      data1[[metric]][data1$species_code == species],
      data2[[metric]][data2$species_code == species]
    ),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  # Left: cruise-level scatterplot
  p_left <- plot_length_scatter(
    data2, species, metric, env_var
  ) +
    labs(
      title = "Cruise-level",
      y = paste0(metric_label, " body length (mm)")
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold")
    )

  # Right: annual bar plot
  p_right <- plot_length_env(
    data1, species, metric, env_data, env_var
  ) +
    labs(
      title = "Annual"
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = y_limits) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
      axis.title.y.left = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y.left = element_blank()
    )

  # Combine
  p_left + p_right +
    plot_layout(widths = widths) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(
        species, ": ", metric_label,
        " body length vs. ", env_label
      ),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 17, face = "bold"))
      )
}
```

## Lags scatter

cruise-level scatter plots with monthly lags:

```{r}
plot_length_lag <- function(data, species, metric, index) {

  lag_vars <- c(index, paste0(index, "_", 1:3))
  lag_labels <- c("No lag", "1-month lag",
                  "2-month lag", "3-month lag")

  metric_label <- ifelse(metric == "median_length", "Median", "Q3")
  env_label <- toupper(index)

  # Prepare data
  plot_df <- data %>%
    filter(species_code == species) %>%
    select(all_of(c(metric, lag_vars))) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(lag_vars),
      names_to = "lag",
      values_to = "env_value"
    ) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(env_value),
      is.finite(.data[[metric]])
    )

  # Create one plot per lag
  plots <- lapply(seq_along(lag_vars), function(i) {

    lag_df <- plot_df %>%
      filter(lag == lag_vars[i])

    # Regression and correlation
    model <- lm(
      reformulate("env_value", response = metric),
      data = lag_df
    )

    intercept <- coef(model)[1]
    slope <- coef(model)[2]

    cor_result <- cor.test(
      lag_df$env_value,
      lag_df[[metric]],
      method = "pearson"
    )

    r <- unname(cor_result$estimate)
    p <- cor_result$p.value

    p_color <- ifelse(p < 0.05, "forestgreen", "#a91b0d")

    # Annotation labels
    eq_label <- paste0(
      "y = ", round(intercept, 2),
      ifelse(slope < 0, " - ", " + "),
      abs(round(slope, 2)), "x"
    )

    r_label <- paste0("r = ", round(r, 3))
    p_label <- paste0(
      "p = ", format.pval(p, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)
    )

    # Scatterplot
    p_scatter <- ggplot(
      lag_df,
      aes(x = env_value, y = .data[[metric]])
    ) +
      geom_point(
        color = species_colors[species],
        size = 2.5,
        alpha = 0.8
      ) +
      geom_smooth(
        method = "lm",
        formula = y ~ x,
        se = TRUE,
        color = env_colors[index],
        fill = env_colors[index],
        alpha = 0.2
      ) +
      labs(
        title = lag_labels[i],
        x = env_label,
        y = paste0(metric_label, " body length (mm)")
      ) +
      theme_classic() +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 11)
      )

    # Annotation panel
    p_stats <- ggplot() +
      annotate(
        "text", x = 0, y = 0.75,
        label = eq_label,
        hjust = 0, size = 4
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text", x = 0, y = 0.55,
        label = r_label,
        hjust = 0, size = 4
      ) +
      annotate(
        "text", x = 0, y = 0.35,
        label = p_label,
        hjust = 0, size = 4,
        color = p_color
      ) +
      xlim(0, 1) +
      ylim(0, 1) +
      theme_void()

    # Combine scatter + statistics
    p_scatter + p_stats +
      patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(4, 1.5))
  })

  # Stack all four plots
  patchwork::wrap_plots(plots, ncol = 1) +
    patchwork::plot_annotation(
      title = paste0(
        species, ": ", metric_label,
        " body length vs. ", env_label
      ),
      theme = theme(
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")
      )
    )
}
```
